rationale:
Evidence: the iteration-0 design (kp 4, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.8, weights -2..2) left the course on all 60 trials across oval, s-bend and slalom. Progress stalled at 0.13 to 0.20, so the robot went off track after roughly 0.6 to 0.9 m. Steering oscillation was high (0.11 to 0.16) and line-loss events occurred in 1 to 2 runs per track. The max_error of about 0.06 is the off-track limit itself, so the robot was diverging, not just wandering.

Diagnosis: the effective steering gain is very high. With kp 4 and weights up to ±2, a single sensor on the tape gives turn up to ±8, which is about ±2800 PWM of wheel differential. Combined with base_speed 1.8 (PWM about 3685), each correction overshoots and the oscillation grows until the tape is lost. Slalom was worst, which fits sharper direction changes amplifying the overshoot.

Changes: (1) kp 4 to 2.5, roughly halving the proportional response so corrections are smaller and less overshoot. (2) kd 0.5 to 0.8 to add damping against the faster signal changes that cause the oscillation. (3) ki 0.1 to 0.05 to limit integral windup on long bends, since the drift is oscillatory, not a steady offset. (4) base_speed 1.8 to 1.5: the robot needs time to correct on bends, and it can still reach about 1.3 to 1.5 m/s on average. Completion inside 3 s is worth less than staying on track, which is worth 500 points. (5) Geometry is kept as before. Sensor spacing already covers the 25 mm tape, and the off-track allowance is capped at 0.06 m regardless of body width, so widening the body gains nothing. Weights and line_loss stay as they were.

Expected result: fewer off-track ends and lower steering oscillation. I expect progress to rise well above 0.2 on the development tracks, with completion possible on oval. Completion time may be about 3.2 to 3.6 s, so the speed term may be lost. The main uncertainty is whether kp 2.5 is too weak for the sharpest slalom bends, which the next round should check.
